ALTERNATIVE METHODS
The City provides the following two alternative methods of viewing and listening to the City Council Meeting

The disruption in service of any alternative method does not preclude the City Council or other legislative body
from taking further action on an agenda item.

Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public may choose to submit comments
electronically for consideration by the City Council or other City Legislative Body by sending them to the City
Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To
ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit

Inglewood, California
  July 9, 2024

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  July 9, 2024, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the City
  Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Finance
  Authority, Parking Authority, and Joint Powers Authority at the hour of 2:01 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/Finance
  Authority Secretary/Parking Authority Secretary/Joint Powers Authority Secretary
  announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman/Finance Authority Chairman/Parking Authority
  Chairman/Joint Powers Authority Chairman, Council
  Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority
  Members/Finance Authority Members/Parking Authority
  Members/Joint Powers Authority Members Gray, Padilla,
  Morales, Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority/Parking
  Authority/Joint Powers Authority officials and personnel present were as follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Mark F. Weinberg  City Manager/ Executive Director*
  Rick R. Olivarez  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Finance Authority,
  Parking Authority, and Joint Powers Authority.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/Finance Authority Chairman/Parking Authority
  Chairman/Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons
  present who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing
  Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers Authority on any item on the
  Agendas.

  There was no response.

142.9  PAYMENT WARRANTS AND BILLS – RECEIVED AND FILED. The demands
  presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated July 3, 2024, in
  the amount of $7,369,596.89, and dated June 28, 2024, in the amount of $6,811,246.40, are
  hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority
  Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said registers that said demands are received
  and filed.

  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman ordered the Warrants and
  Bills received and filed.

  Council Member Morales requested that the Minutes for April 9, 2024, be pulled.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Faulk, and seconded by Council Member
  Padilla that the Minutes for the City Council Meetings held on April 16, 2024, April 23,
  2024, and April 30, 2024, be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.
 July 9, 2024

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Faulk, and seconded by Mayor Butts that
  the Minutes for the City Council Meeting held on April 9, 2024, be approved. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Abstain: Council Member Morales.

132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending the
  following:
  A. Reject Claims pursuant to Government Code, Section 913:
  1. Schuyler Jackson for alleged personal injury/property damage; dangerous condition
  roadway design on September 4, 2023.
  2. Ilesia Jones for alleged tire damage; pothole on February 22, 2024.
  3. Kathleen Jones for alleged tire damage; pothole on March 30, 2023.
  4. Antonio Novoa for alleged personal injury/property damage; road obstruction (debris
  placed in street by Contractor, The Right Choice) on January 11, 2024.
  5. Curtis Preston for alleged personal injury; forcefully removed from assigned seat
  (1001 Stadium Drive) on October 29, 2023.
  6. Curtis Preston for alleged personal injury; to remove PTSD; witnessed father
  forcefully be removed from seat and escorted out the stadium at/near 1001 Stadium
  Drive on October 29, 2023.
  7. Maria Ramos De Castillo for alleged personal injury; uneven sidewalk on January 19,
  2024.
  8. Matthew Torres for alleged personal injury; assaulted by security guards and/or
  employee – 1001 S. Stadium Drive on October 1, 2023.
  9. Lorenzo Wilkinson for alleged tire damage; pothole on February 29, 2024.
  B. Reject Amended Claims pursuant to Government Code, Section 913:
  1. Tayon Blockmon for alleged personal injury; false imprisonment, excessive force on
  February 4, 2024.
  2. Ulyssess Kinard for alleged personal injury, City failed to take measures to protect
  citizens in high crime area (shot by unknown assailant) on October 7, 2023.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Reject Claims listed as A-1 through A-9; and 2) Reject
  Amended Claims listed as B-1 and B-2. The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

142  AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO AGREEMENT NO. 22-233 APPROVED – VESTIS
  SERVICES, LLC. Staff report dated July 9, 2024, was presented recommending that the
  Mayor and Council Members approve Amendment No. 1 to Agreement No. 22-233 with
  Vestis Services, LLC, extending the term to June 30, 2025, and reflecting the Contractor’s
  change in business name to Vestis Services, LLC.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby approve Amendment No. 1 to Agreement No. 22-233. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

131.9  AGREEMENT NO. 24-278 APPROVED – RSG, INC. Staff report dated July 9, 2024,
  was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council Members approve a one-year
  agreement (with the option to extend two (2) additional one-year terms) with RSG, Inc., to
  provide specialized administrative services to the Housing Protection Department for the
  preparation of the Rental Housing Board and its associated duties regarding petitions and
  appeals.

  2
 July 9, 2024

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 24-278 in an amount not to exceed
  $100,000. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  RESOLUTION NO. 24-102 ADOPTED - AMENDING THE 2023-2024 OPERATING
  BUDGET. Staff report dated July 9, 2024, was presented recommending that the Mayor
  and Council Members adopt a resolution amending the Fiscal Year 2023-2024 Operating
  Budget, in an amount not to exceed $590,252.15, to fund the Pedestrian Improvement
  Project.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  Resolution No. 24-102 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFONIA, AMENDING THE 2023-2024 ANNUAL BUDGET TO FUND
  THE PEDESTRIAN IMPROVEMENT PROJECT

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  REPORTS – CITY CLERK. City Clerk Aisha L. Thompson enthusiastically spoke about
  the State of the City Economic Summit, describing it as a fabulous, fantastic, and
  extraordinary event. She expressed her gratitude to the Mayor, Sharis Rhodes, Maria
  Barbara, and everyone involved in making the State of the City a success. The City Clerk
  also extended a special thank you to PY Tenders for their hospitality, highlighting their
  respectful treatment of all attendees regardless of their title or position. She emphasized PY
  Tenders' outstanding performance at the State of the City and recommended them for future
  City events. Additionally, she mentioned Councilwoman Faulk's Jazz Festival, noting the
  Mayor, Council Members, and grateful residents in attendance. She commended
  Councilwoman Faulk's vision and encouraged her to continue contributing to the City and
  community, expressing her happiness in participating in it.

126  MONTHLY TREASURER’S REPORT. Staff report dated July 9, 2024, was presented
  submitting the Monthly Treasurer’s Report for the Month ending May 31, 2024.

  Mayor Butts ordered the report received and filed.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished
  to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not elsewhere
  considered on the Agenda.

  Brandee Keith, South Coast Air Quality Management District Representative, invited the
  Council and residents to their 10th Annual Environment Justice Conference on October 24,
  2024, at the Town & Gown University of Southern California. She noted that registration is
  mandatory and can be completed on their website.

  Charlene Sanders, a resident of District 1, thanked Council Member Gray for organizing
  the community meeting. She mentioned that the meeting was very informative and she
  appreciated the opportunity to speak with the Chief of Police. Charlene also mentioned
  addressing some issues on her street, Buckthorn, and expressed satisfaction with the City's
  management of traffic. She noted that her birthday was on July 10th and shared gifts with
  everyone present, symbolizing her representation. Finally, she stated that she was the same
  age as the President and emphasized that there was nothing wrong with his mind.

  Mayor Butts left the dais at the hour of 2:10 p.m.

  Mayor Butts returned to the dais at the hour of 2:11 p.m.

  3
 July 9, 2024

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts thanked Sharis Rhodes, Maria
  Barbara, Kathy Ares, Parrish Gibson, Passion Schoolfield, Alicia Fong, Alethia McCann-
  Scott, Halimah Ginyard, and Tracy Shields-Johnson for their assistance with the Economic
  Summit 2024, extending his condolences to Leslie and Carla Smalls, daughters of Winne
  Smith, and declared the meeting adjourned in the memory of Andy Knacker, and Winnie
  Smith, at the hour of 2:37 p.m.

  Approved this 17th day of September, 2024.
  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
